scope: The proposed loss-only absorption of the spatial-large-field complement is rigorously ruled out for the actual Wilson source, not merely for a toy law. For any measurable endpoint region E and continuous f vanishing outside E, endpoint symmetry gives loss(f)/2<=R_E(f). Every nonconstant continuous f has strictly positive actual transfer variance loss at finite cutoff. The physical bump f=max(0,D-t), D=2-Re(character(spatialHolonomy(0,0,1))), is supported on the actual large-plaquette event E={D>t}, is nonconstant for 0<=t<4 on periods n>1, and is gauge invariant. Consequently no bound R_E(f)<=epsilon*loss(f) can hold for all physical f when epsilon<1/2. For 0<=delta<2, E={D>delta^2} lies in the spatial-large-field complement of the two-field axial FlatBox region. That exact excluded source also retains at least half the bump loss, ruling out the proposed uniform small coefficient for this complement. A valid replacement is proved: R_E(f)<=2*loss(chi*f)+cutoffCost(chi,f), for chi=1 on E. The cutoff cost retains the actual two-endpoint density and f(w)^2*(chi(v)-chi(w))^2; ground weighting gives the existing correlated density J exactly. A concrete continuous physical cutoff equals one above D>t, vanishes below D<=t/2 and lies in [0,1]. Neither the localized loss nor cutoff cost is numerically absorbed. Distant mixed-ground summability, global physical coercivity and continuum Yang-Mills remain open.
